general.title: General
general.html:
This section defines the basic structure of the game.

  • N Columns controls the board width.
  • N Rows controls the board height.
  • Win / Lose changes the main goal: you can play normal Ta-Te-Ti or misère mode, where completing a line makes you lose.
  • N in a row defines how many aligned pieces activate the condition.

pieces.title: Pieces
pieces.html:
This section controls how many pieces each player can have and what happens when a piece must move.

  • Unlimited disabled: each player has a limited number of live pieces.
  • Unlimited enabled: players can keep adding pieces without limit.
  • Forced: when reaching the maximum, the next action must move the oldest piece.
  • Limit: when reaching the maximum, the next action must move any of your pieces.
  • Free: with limited pieces, you can move any of your pieces at any time, even before placing all possible pieces.
  • Blocked: with unlimited pieces, you can't move a piece that's already on the board.
  • Free: with unlimited pieces, you can choose to move one of your pieces instead of placing a new one.

The number above each piece shows its current order among that player's pieces.

holes.title: Rupture
holes.html:
When a piece leaves a cell, that cell can become broken (blocked).

  • The title toggle enables or disables rupture.
  • If disabled, the cell becomes empty when the piece leaves.
  • If enabled, the abandoned cell becomes broken.
  • Unlimited: the break lasts until the end of the match (turn count does not apply).
  • Without unlimited, Turns is the base duration (minimum 1).
  • Per player multiplies that amount by the number of players in the game.

gravity.title: Gravity
gravity.html:
Gravity pulls pieces toward one side of the board (like a sideways Connect 4).

  • The title toggle enables or disables this mechanic.
  • Initial direction sets which way is “down” at the start of the match.
  • With vertical gravity (up/down), tap any empty cell in that column: the new piece settles at the landing spot (strong arrow). Fainter arrows mark other empty cells in the same column you can use as shortcuts.
  • With horizontal gravity (left/right), the same idea applies along the row.
  • When moving a piece, tap any empty cell on the board; the piece is placed there, then gravity pulls it and the other pieces along the current direction.
  • Broken cells from rupture block movement through that cell.
  • Rotate gravity changes the pull direction every N completed turns; there is a one-second pause so you can see the board, then all pieces re-settle in the new direction.
  • Rotation step is 90°, 180°, or 270° per tick (or random among those).
  • Turn direction is clockwise or counter-clockwise on the screen (or random each tick).
  • Per player multiplies N by the number of players, same idea as rupture duration.

players.title: Players
players.html:
Set how many players join and customize their emojis.

  • Number uses the first players in list order.
  • With more than two in Lose mode, completing a line removes a player from the turn order; enable Eliminate losers to also remove their pieces from the board.
  • With more than two in Win mode, the first line wins unless Continue for ranking is enabled, where winners are removed until the full order is decided.
  • With Continue for ranking on, Eliminate winners clears that player's pieces from the board when they take a round; turn it off to leave their pieces as obstacles.
